facts.claim: Python is an easy to learn, powerful programming language.
When the Python interpreter is called with a file name argument, it reads and executes a script from that file.

On Windows, Python is obtained through the Python install manager, which can be installed from the Microsoft Store or from python.org/downloads; after it is installed, typing python in a terminal gets you started.
The Windows page has a Troubleshooting section for when the python or py commands do not seem to work.
Python for macOS is distributed as installer packages from the python.org downloads page.
Recent versions of macOS include a python3 command in /usr/bin/python3 that links to an older, incomplete Python used by Apple's development tools, which should never be modified or deleted.
The default options of the python.org installer ensure that its python3 is used instead of the system python3.
pip supports installing packages from PyPI.
The official Python tutorial is published in the Python 3 documentation at docs.python.org/3/.
FastAPI is a modern, fast (high-performance) web framework for building APIs with Python based on standard Python type hints.
When managing the environment and packages manually, create and activate a virtual environment, then install FastAPI with pip install "fastapi[standard]".
python -m venv creates a virtual environment in the given directory, with a bin subdirectory on POSIX and a Scripts subdirectory on Windows.

Activating a virtual environment runs its activation script (source <venv>/bin/activate on POSIX, <venv>\Scripts\activate.bat on Windows) and prepends its directory to PATH, so that running python invokes the environment's interpreter.
On Microsoft Windows, PowerShell may require the Activate.ps1 script to be enabled by setting the execution policy for the user.
fastapi dev main.py reads the file, detects the FastAPI app in it and starts a development server using Uvicorn.
The FastAPI home page example shows the server at http://127.0.0.1:8000 and the interactive API documentation at /docs.
python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt writes the installed packages to a requirements file, which python -m pip install -r requirements.txt installs from.
By default, fastapi dev starts with auto-reload enabled, which reloads the server when code changes.
The server output shows 'Uvicorn running' with '(Press CTRL+C to quit)'.
The /docs page is the automatic interactive API documentation provided by Swagger UI.
The FastAPI development server is started with fastapi dev and prints the address http://127.0.0.1:8000, where it can be stopped with CTRL+C.
The last line of the error message indicates what happened; the exception type is printed as part of the message.
ModuleNotFoundError is a subclass of ImportError which is raised by import when a module could not be located.
Node.js is an asynchronous event-driven JavaScript runtime.
The Python Tutorial is the official tutorial for the Python language, published by the Python project.
The FastAPI tutorial shows how to install FastAPI and build an app with it, step by step.
